title: Delayed claims ingestion after partner format change

evidence.text: At 09:12, the Northlake feed's visible processing lag rose from 40 seconds to 18 minutes; other partner feeds stayed below 55 seconds.
At 09:10, the partner circuit breaker opened after the worker failure ratio crossed its configured threshold and stopped new Northlake deliveries for six minutes.
During the open interval, the Northlake broker partition depth stopped increasing, while already leased messages continued to retry.
Worker profiles from 09:08 through 09:24 show most CPU time in recursive normalization of nested attachment metadata; profiles from unaffected partitions do not.
Northlake began sending a previously unused optional `relatedAttachments` field at 09:07. The envelope schema permits that field and does not constrain its nesting depth.
Quarantine writes increased after the worker-side depth guard rejected envelopes deeper than 32 levels; every sampled rejection contained nested `relatedAttachments`.
In staging, replaying sampled Northlake envelopes with the optional field removed completed normally; replaying the original samples reproduced high CPU and the depth-guard rejection.
Operators forced the breaker closed at 09:31. Input throughput briefly rose, worker CPU reached 100%, and lag across two previously healthy partner partitions began increasing.
After the breaker was reopened at 09:36, healthy-partition lag returned toward baseline while Northlake events remained paused or quarantined.
Metadata lookup latency rose from 80 ms to 900 ms between 09:14 and 09:20, including requests from services unrelated to claims ingestion.
For failed Northlake attempts, traces spend less than 3% of elapsed time in metadata lookup calls and most elapsed time before the lookup span begins.
A worker deployment completed at 08:50. Its release notes list logging and metric-label changes; no artifact-to-artifact binary comparison was retained.
Broker dashboards report a leader election at 09:11, but broker logs show no unavailable partition and consumers of unrelated topics report no processing gap.
With Northlake intake paused, increasing the worker pool from 20 to 35 reduced the existing retry backlog but did not allow any sampled deeply nested envelope to complete.
The gateway validator checks types and required fields before publishing; depth is enforced only by the worker guard because no gateway depth limit is configured.

The incident record contains no controlled replay of pre-09:07 Northlake traffic on the current worker artifact and no replay of the nested samples on the prior artifact. It also does not record whether a quarantine write removes the corresponding broker message from retry eligibility.

hypotheses.text: Northlake envelope structure drives excessive normalization work in enrichment workers.
The partner circuit breaker creates the worker failures observed for Northlake traffic.
Metadata lookup latency drives the worker failures observed for Northlake traffic.
The 08:50 worker artifact changes how enrichment handles the affected envelopes.
Broker leader movement drives the Northlake processing failure.

edges.relation: worker failures contribute to threshold crossing
open state limits new feed deliveries
lookup latency accounts for most failed-attempt duration
leader movement interrupts affected message consumption
rejected envelopes are separated from the retry path
open state initiates recursive normalization failures

actions.text: Keep Northlake intake isolated while preserving breaker and quarantine telemetry.
Add a bounded nesting rule at ingress and coordinate rejected-record handling with Northlake.
Force the partner breaker closed and disable the worker depth guard until the backlog clears.
Cap normalization work and replay quarantined samples in a limited canary before resuming intake.
Roll back the 08:50 worker artifact before conducting further comparisons.
Increase metadata lookup capacity and resume Northlake intake without other changes.
